question: A cistern has a hole at the bottom through which water leaks. A tap can fill the cistern in 7 hours and the hole at the bottom can empty the fully filled cistern in 8 hours. If both the tap and the hole are open, then what will be the time taken to completely fill the empty cistern?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net work = Fill − Empty = 1/7 − 1/8

= (8 − 7) / 56 = 1/56

So time = 56 hours

**∴ Answer = 56 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Tap fills in 7 hours

Hole empties in 8 hours

**Formula used:**

Net efficiency = Fill rate − Empty rate

 
 

 Tap/Hole
 Hours
 Total Work
 Efficiency
 
 
 
 

 Tap (Fill)
 7
 56
 8
 
 

 Hole (Empty)
 8
 −7
 
 

 

Calculation:

⇒ Net efficiency = 8 − 7 = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Total work = 56 units

⇒ Time = 56 ÷ 1 = 56 hours

∴ The correct answer is 56 hours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes Concept

Filling is positive work, emptying is negative work.

LCM Method

Take total work as LCM of times to simplify efficiency calculation.

Net Work Formula

Net rate = Sum of individual rates considering signs.
